body:
Suggested replacement SQL query:

```sql
            SELECT
                cons.conname as name,
                right(left(pg_get_constraintdef(cons.oid), -1), -7) as src
            FROM
                pg_catalog.pg_constraint cons
            WHERE
                cons.conrelid = :table_oid AND
                cons.contype = 'c'
```

The left and right functions strip off the `CHECK ( ... )` that is returned by the `pg_get_constraintdef` function.
do you know offhand how far back that function is available on PG ?

It looks like it goes right back to version 8.0:

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/8.0/functions-info.html
we are already stripping from the text returned so ill just do more of a proper regex on the python side.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Use pg_get_constraintdef for CHECK constraint reflection** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1113

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_2** branch:

**Use pg_get_constraintdef for CHECK constraint reflection** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1114

I wondered if the existing test should be updated so that the present code will fail. I found this issue because of the mismatch between the constraints reported by PGAdmin and the values in the `consrc` column.

I have posted a suggestion (untried) below that inserts bad data into the consrc column.  I don't know the best way to handle the fact that this insertion will fail in PG 12 because the column will no longer exist.

```python
    @testing.provide_metadata
    def test_reflect_check_constraint(self):
        meta = self.metadata

        cc_table = Table(
            "pgsql_cc",
            meta,
            Column("a", Integer()),
            CheckConstraint("a > 1 AND a < 5", name="cc1"),
            CheckConstraint("a = 1 OR (a > 2 AND a < 5)", name="cc2"),
        )

        cc_table.create()

        # Insert bad data into pg_constraint.consrc column, which should not be used
        # and which will be deprecated in PG 12
        CONSRC_SQL = """"
            UPDATE pg_catalog.pg_constraint
            SET consrc = 'consrc column is deprecated'
            WHERE contype = 'c'
        """
        try:
            with testing.db.connect() as conn:
                conn.execute(CONSRC_SQL)
        except SomeKindOfPsycopg2ErrorMaybeProgrammingError:
            # consrc column doesn't exist in PG > 12
            pass   

        reflected = Table("pgsql_cc", MetaData(testing.db), autoload=True)

        check_constraints = dict(
            (uc.name, uc.sqltext.text)
            for uc in reflected.constraints
            if isinstance(uc, CheckConstraint)
        )

        eq_(
            check_constraints,
            {
                u"cc1": u"(a > 1) AND (a < 5)",
                u"cc2": u"(a = 1) OR ((a > 2) AND (a < 5))",
            },
        )
```
I'm not sure you can update pg_catalog tables directly?    what are we looking for in that test?

I don't know if you can update those tables or not either. The aim was to show that the constraint definition was coming from wherever `pg_get_constraintdef` looks, and not from the `consrc` column.

Thanks for fixing this.
ah OK.   Well we have CI where we just run these databases for real so I'll add pg 12 when it's released.

This def contained the faulty code that was supposed to have been replaced in rel. 1.2
using the consrc column.

Introduced the proposed fix from issue #4463 in this source and tested again: magic!

checked the repo here https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/rel_1_3/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/base.py

This code is the correct logic using pg_get_constraintdef

Also checked code source here https://pypi.org/project/SQLAlchemy/#files
which is also correct.

Very confusing since the steps I did on my system was doing a fresh install of sqlalchemy (no newer version was ever present on this system), it reports version 1.3.13 and still it holds the code containing the deprecated column name.

issue.title: Use pg_get_constraintdef for CHECK constraint reflection
